knowledgePattern: Bound an exponential reciprocal sum before optimising a reciprocal quadratic

hints.title: Name the repeated sum
hints.body: Use the whole expression 2x+2−x as a variable. Square it to connect it with the other two powers.
hints.recap: Squaring a sum includes a cross term; a useful substitution keeps the repeated expression together.
hints.pitfall: Do not omit the cross term when squaring.
hints.pause: Rewrite the denominator as a quadratic in the new variable.

recall.reminder: Squaring a sum includes a cross term; a useful substitution keeps the repeated expression together.

hints.title: Prove its allowed range
hints.body: Put u=2x>0. Compare u+1/u with a constant by bringing terms over a common positive denominator and looking for a square.
hints.recap: Optimisation must respect the exact attainable range of the inner quantity.
hints.pitfall: The formal vertex of the denominator might not be attainable.
hints.pause: Find an attained lower bound for the inner quantity, then minimise the denominator on that range.

recall.reminder: Optimisation must respect the exact attainable range of the inner quantity.

solution:
1. Let t=2x+2−x. Squaring gives 4x+4−x=t2−2, so the denominator is t2−2t+6=(t−1)2+5.

2. For u=2x>0, we have u+1/u−2=(u−1)2/u≥0. Thus t≥2, with equality at x=0.

3. On this permitted range, (t−1)2≥1, so the positive denominator is at least 6. Its reciprocal is at most 1/6, and x=0 attains it. Answer B.
